admission.justification: The narrower trigger, branch tips only, was offered with its consequence and declined, and every memory route's refusal now depends on this one fact about the repository.

alternatives.option: The lock holds once the memory repository holds converted memory anywhere: a local branch tip, or a registered worktree's working tree, that holds knowledge/layout.json. No switch, flag or install-time state.
alternatives.reason: It is a fact about the repository, so the lock is live from the installation, is scoped per memory repository, and never locks another code repository's memory.

alternatives.option: Only a branch tip that holds the marker locks the repository.
alternatives.reason: The lock would start only at the converting leaf's first memory commit that holds the conversion, and that conversion stays uncommitted until the leaf's closeout.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Uncommitted converted worktrees outside a converting leaf have to be allowed in a live memory repository.

consequences: A route asks the lock only after it has decided that its memory is unconverted on every side; a converting candidate holds the marker and is gated, never locked.
One converted branch tip or registered worktree locks every unconverted line of that memory repository, for every session on the machine.
A probe Git cannot answer refuses by name; only a directory that is definitely no repository reads as unlocked.
context: Unconverted memory must be refused at every write, check, sync, closeout and landing route once the cutover build is installed (MIK-R09 rule 6, MIK-R24 rule 9). The lock had to stay inert for a memory repository that never converted, and be live from the installation although the converting leaf's conversion stays uncommitted until that leaf's closeout (MIK-R37 rule 2).
